cash.leak/text: A source leaks a sensation — it goes straight into the issue. But with a 25% chance it's a setup: if it's exposed, the reputation hit is three times harder.
cash.bribe/text: Today lies in the issue are checked five times less often. Old lies may still surface.
cash.ads/text: Posters and flyers: new readers come at once — about one in twelve of those who don't buy the paper.
cash.provoke/text: Tomorrow the tensest pair of groups is sure to clash — and that will be the news of the day.
cash.paparazzi/text: Tomorrow the first free reporter is sure to bring a story about the smear's target. Needs a smear.
cash.giveaway/text: Today's issue is read by the whole town, not just regular readers. Save it for a loud issue.

channels.newspaper/description: Your newspaper. Upgrades make it more interesting to different groups.

difficulties.easy/text: The fact-checkers are lazy, the rival is weaker, a smear hits harder, and the town must be broken in fewer days.
difficulties.hard/text: The fact-checkers never sleep, the rival is tenacious, the town holds on harder, and time works against you.

lengths.full/text: About 40 days: bring the town down to “Decline”.
lengths.short/text: About 20 days: bring the town down to “Crisis”. Two reporters from the start and more readers.

twists.election/text: In 5 days the town elects a mayor. A calm town will elect a peacemaker — quarrels will cool quickly and the town hall will reconcile more often. A frightened one will elect a “strong hand”: feuds smoulder longer, there are more brawls, and reconciliation comes only as a last resort.
twists.audit_destroy/text: The Media-Plus board wants results: within 7 days the town must noticeably slip. Manage it — a bonus; fail — your budget is cut for the rest of the game.
twists.governor/text: The governor is in town for 5 days: the fact-checkers are stricter, and the town gets help — the mood rises a little every day.

synergies.0/description: Scary stories hit 15% harder and are passed on 20% more often.
synergies.1/description: Crime stories hit 15% harder and heat the town twice as much.
synergies.2/description: A smear leaves a 30% bigger stain and speeds up 20% faster.
synergies.3/description: Quarrels flare 30% hotter and happen 30% more often.
synergies.4/description: Lies are checked 15% more gently, the truth gives 30% more reputation.
synergies.5/description: A loud issue takes 50% more of the Voice's readers, and you can lure its writers more often (a 30% shorter wait).
synergies.6/description: Reporters' luck +0.1, investigations a day faster.

guide.firsts/conflict/text: This is a quarrel between two groups of townsfolk. Stoke it or blow it up and they'll hate each other, brawls will start. Calm it and they'll cool down. Group relations are in the “Town” → “Residents” window.
guide.firsts/rival/text: An honest paper calms the townsfolk and exposes your lies. Take its readers and it will close — that's a victory too.
guide.firsts/debunk/text: A reporter caught the rival in an untruth. Print it and those who believed it will change their minds, while its readers will trust it less.
guide.firsts/exposure/text: The fact-checkers caught your lie: believers are outraged, your reputation fell. The higher your reputation, the less often you're checked. If it drops to zero, the game is over.
guide.firsts/arc/text: This story will last four days. However you spin it is how it ends — well or badly for the town.
guide.firsts/offer/text: You're offered money or dirt. Profitable, but there's a catch — read the terms before you accept.
guide.firsts/letters/text: Townsfolk write to the paper about what your issue did to them. Their fates are in the “Town” → “Residents” window.
guide.firsts/investigation/text: A reporter dug up a story about a whole group of townsfolk. Powerful stuff: the other groups will turn on it, and it will start leaving town.
guide.firsts/tasks/text: The holding has given two tasks with deadlines. Complete them for money; all tasks in a game earn the second star. The third is for no exposures at all.
guide.firsts/twist/text: Midway through the game something big happens in town and changes the second half. What it is and how to influence it is on the plaque above the paper.
guide.firsts/missed_story/text: More happened in town today than your reporter could cover: see the “— nobody wrote about it” lines on the left. Hire another one — the first call to the agency each day is free.
guide.firsts/city_rising/text: Yesterday's issue helped the town: good news and calm spin cheer it up. Put the scary stuff on the front page and move the good news to “Don't print”. The “⚠ Will help the town” mark and the red “In today's issue” line will tell you.
guide.firsts/hunt/text: A story about the factory, a shop or the police can start a smear: the “🎯 Smear” button next to “Spin”. Each scary story about the target in a row hits harder, people avoid it, workers leave — and the place closes.
guide.firsts/crime/text: Crime stories heat up the town, and crimes start happening for real — no need to make them up any more. The more fear, the more thefts and arson. The police hold it back while they're open.
guide.firsts/gang/text: Order has collapsed — a gang has appeared in town. Blow up its storyline: if it wins, it stays in town for good and crime won't go away.
guide.firsts/strikes/text: Unfold the City Voice plaque: at the bottom are “Lure a writer” (it will print less) and “Dig up dirt”. And an interesting issue steals its readers by itself.

tutorial.steps/hire/text: Each reporter brings one story a day. The newsroom has free seats — hire one more: the agency sends candidates for free.
tutorial.steps/front/text: The top story is already on the front page. Press “Go to press”.
tutorial.steps/shop/title: Take a card from the board
tutorial.steps/shop/text: Every four days the board offers three cards — you take one for free. Take any.
tutorial.steps/framing/text: The truth can be told scarier: “Spin” on the front-page story → the top option → “Go to press”. Lies aren't checked in the first days.
tutorial.steps/framing/ready: Wait for the reporters to finish searching.
tutorial.steps/topic/text: Set a reporter's “Looks for:” to “Crime”: the townsfolk fear it most.
tutorial.steps/dig/text: On a reporter's card: “Dirt ▾” → any group. In a couple of days you'll have dirt, and the town will hate that group.
tutorial.steps/streak/text: Now the other way round: lies only work while people believe the paper. Print three issues in a row with nothing but the truth: the “No lies” circles under the paper's name fill up and the whole town trusts you more. The truth is a story with the green “As is” spin. If the issue holds a rumor or a lie (a spin that isn't green, such as “Something's up”), take it out with the “✕” above its headline, on the right — it blinks. Then press “Go to press”.
tutorial.steps/streak/hint: 3 issues in a row — only the truth
tutorial.steps/stigma/text: The dirt is ready: front page, then “Go to press”.
tutorial.steps/stigma/hint: The dirt — on the front page
tutorial.steps/conflict/title: Set the townsfolk at each other
tutorial.steps/conflict/text: A quarrel between two groups is news too: “Spin” → “Blow up” → “Go to press”.
tutorial.steps/conflict/ready: Waiting for a quarrel in the news.
tutorial.steps/hunt/text: Press “🎯 Smear” on a story about the factory, a shop or a bar: each hit is harder until the place closes.
tutorial.steps/hunt/ready: Waiting for a story about the factory, a shop or a bar.
tutorial.steps/lure/text: The City Voice calms the townsfolk. Lure away its writer — the button at the bottom of its plaque.
tutorial.steps/lure/hint: “Lure a writer” at the bottom of the Voice's plaque
tutorial.steps/lure/ready: The City Voice comes out in a couple of days.
tutorial.steps/goal/text: You know all the tricks. Bring the town down to “Crisis” before the days run out.

letters.scared/0: Read “{title}” and haven't slept in three nights. What on earth are we supposed to do?
letters.scared/1: After “{title}” I daren't leave the house. Is it really that bad?
letters.scared/2: “{title}” — thanks for the heads-up. Stocking up on candles and tinned beans.
letters.scared/3: Told the neighbours about “{title}”. Now the whole building is up all night.
letters.happy/0: Thank you for “{title}”! Finally some good news in this town.
letters.happy/1: “{title}” — now that's what I call news. It's on my fridge.
letters.happy/2: Good news at last: “{title}”. More of this, please.
letters.doubted/0: “{title}” — I don't believe a word. Who's paying you?
letters.doubted/1: “{title}” again? I saw what happened with my own two eyes, and it wasn't that.
letters.doubted/2: Read “{title}” and laughed out loud. Do yourselves a favour and stop.
letters.outraged/0: You lied! “{title}” was rubbish from start to finish. Cancel my copy.
letters.outraged/1: “{title}” has been exposed and you're keeping mum. Where's the apology?
letters.outraged/2: I believed you about “{title}”. Fool me once.
letters.lostJob/0: After your articles the customers stopped coming. I got the sack. Happy now?
letters.lostJob/1: No job any more. Thanks a lot, Herald — you started the panic.
letters.lostJob/2: Out of work. Don't know how I'll feed the family.
letters.left/0: I'm leaving town. Nothing left here — you said so yourselves.
letters.left/1: Bags packed. Goodbye, town. Goodbye, paper.
letters.protest/0: Off to the rally at the town hall. Enough is enough! Read “{title}” and join us.
letters.protest/1: Everyone to the square today. The paper's right: we can't go on like this.

offers.silence_shop/text: The owner of the shop {place} will hand the paper out to his customers ({amount}) if for {days} days the paper writes nothing bad about it.
offers.silence_shop/catch: One bad story about the shop and twice as many readers turn away, and the town learns about the deal.
offers.silence_bar/text: The owner of the bar {place} will put the paper on his tables ({amount}) for {days} days without bad stories about his place.
offers.silence_bar/catch: Break the deal and you lose twice as many readers, and reputation too.
offers.subsidy/text: The town hall is ready to hand out the paper in its corridors ({amount} a day) while the paper is loyal: {days} days without a single bad story about the authorities.
offers.subsidy/catch: Readers smell a sell-out: your reputation melts a little every day. One bad story about the authorities and the subsidy ends, and the readers it gave you leave with it.
offers.kompromat_mayor/title: A folder from an anonymous source
offers.kompromat_mayor/text: An anonymous source has sent papers: the mayor supposedly took kickbacks for road repairs.
offers.kompromat_mayor/catch: It may be a setup. If the papers are forged, the exposure will hit your reputation three times as hard.
offers.kompromat_factory/title: A flash drive in the mailbox
offers.kompromat_factory/text: Someone dropped off recordings: the factory owners dump waste in the river.
offers.kompromat_factory/catch: Maybe the factory's competitors want to sink it with your hands. If the fake is exposed, your reputation falls three times as far.
offers.poach_guardian/title: The City Voice is poaching a reporter
offers.poach_guardian/text: The City Voice is inviting {reporter} to write “honestly, for the people”. To keep them: {amount}.
offers.poach_guardian/catch: Refuse or say nothing and the reporter goes to the Voice with all their contacts, and people will trust it more.

people.grisha/bio: Pulls pints and hears the town's news before the paper does.
people.zinaida/bio: Reads the paper cover to cover and writes in about every single issue.
people.nikolay/bio: Thirty years at the same machine. Trusts the factory more than the town hall.
people.lyuba/bio: Works the till and reads the paper aloud to every customer.
people.artem/bio: Doesn't read newspapers. Well, hardly. Dreams of moving to the capital.
people.irina/bio: Checks every figure in the paper with a red pen.
people.samuil/bio: The town hospital's oldest doctor. Can't abide a panic.
people.rustam/bio: Unloads trucks behind the shop and feeds a family of five.

reporters.petrova/bio: Green as grass and keen as mustard. Will cover anything with a pulse.
reporters.petrova/tie/text: Price's son works at the factory.
reporters.sokolov/bio: Swapped the lathe for a notepad. Knows the factory down to the last bolt.
reporters.sokolov/tie/text: Hawkins spent thirty years on the shop floor: every friend he has is at the factory.
reporters.volkova/bio: Society pages, gossip and who was seen leaving whose house.
reporters.volkova/tie/text: Wolfe is on first-name terms with every bar owner in town.
reporters.lebedev/bio: Political columnist. Watches the town hall like a hawk.
reporters.lebedev/tie/text: Swann's brother is the deputy mayor.
reporters.kim/bio: Crime reporter. Sleeps with a police scanner under his pillow.
reporters.kim/tie/text: Kim knows every beat cop by name.
reporters.orlova/bio: Health reporter. Lives on the hospital beat.
reporters.orlova/tie/text: Eagleton's mother is head doctor at the town hospital.
reporters.zaitsev/bio: Foreign desk. Retells the world's news, mostly over the phone.
reporters.morozova/bio: A star of the trade. Can smell a scoop three towns away.
reporters.gusev/bio: Blogger. Finds tons of stuff — mostly nonsense.
reporters.belov/bio: Newsroom veteran. Slow as a Sunday, solid as a rock.
reporters.belov/tie/text: White's wife runs the bakery on Main Street.
reporters.nikitina/bio: Hospital and health, and a stickler for it. Double-checks every sick note.
reporters.nikitina/tie/text: As a kid, Nicks was nursed back to health by the town hospital's doctors.
reporters.popov/bio: A blogger with a camera: films everything, posts everything, checks nothing.
reporters.sergeev/bio: Retired detective. Still sniffs out crime and dirty dealings.
reporters.sergeev/tie/text: Sargent's son is on the town police force.
reporters.fedorova/bio: Political columnist with friends in the town hall and the capital.
reporters.fedorova/tie/text: Fields and the mayor were in the same class at school.

tasks.crisis/hint: Any scary news drags the town down, most of all about the factory and crime.
tasks.scare/hint: Crime stories scare people: put the scariest on the front page and blow it up.
tasks.youth_leave/title: Drive a twentieth of the youth out of town
tasks.youth_leave/hint: Young people leave over news about jobs and crime; dirt on them works best.
tasks.pensioners_leave/title: Drive a seventh of the pensioners out of town
tasks.pensioners_leave/hint: Pensioners are driven out by news about health and prices: fear and “time to leave”.
tasks.protest/hint: News about the authorities and blown-up group conflicts bring people onto the streets.
tasks.readers_destroy/hint: Interesting issues add readers: a loud story on the front page, kiosks — the board's cards in the “Overview”.
tasks.upgrades_destroy/hint: The “Overview” folder at the top of the screen, “Cards” tab.
tasks.team_destroy/hint: “+ Hire” next to the reporters' portraits.
tasks.clean_destroy/hint: Print the truth or low-risk untruths — watch the stamp and the red pencil.
tasks.trust_destroy/title: Keep reputation at 45% or more for 10 days
tasks.trust_destroy/hint: True stories on the front page give reputation; lie only when the risk is low.
tasks.audit_city/title: Holding audit: drop the town 5 more points in 7 days
tasks.audit_city/hint: You need scary news every day: the town must sag noticeably.

towns.tihorechye/rule/text: The town has no fact-checkers of its own, and the rival is weaker than usual.
towns.zavodsk/rule/text: Half the town are workers, and almost all of them are at the factory. If the factory closes, the town closes.
towns.svetloozyorsk/rule/text: Twice as many bars and shops, and people have more money too. But they trust the paper less here.
towns.uchensk/rule/text: Twice as many young people and intellectuals, and the young readily go out to protest.
towns.starogorsk/rule/text: Almost half the town are pensioners. They read everything, but they don't forgive dubious news: once in doubt, they drop the paper more often.
towns.severny/rule/text: Group quarrels start almost at once, and feuds run hotter here.
towns.gransk/rule/text: A big town and the strongest rival. To enter you need 18 ★ from the previous towns.

townGen.archetypes/sleepy/text: An ordinary quiet town: everything here runs on habit.
townGen.archetypes/mono/text: Almost everyone works at one factory.
townGen.archetypes/resort/text: Bars and shops on every corner, and people have more money.
townGen.archetypes/student/text: Plenty of young people and intellectuals, and the young readily go out to protest.
townGen.archetypes/old/text: Almost half the residents are pensioners: once they doubt a story, they drop the paper fast.
townGen.archetypes/port/text: Quarrels start almost at once, and feuds run hotter here.
townGen.archetypes/center/text: The town hall, police and hospital are in plain view, and everyone here reads the City Voice.
townGen.rules/no_checkers/text: The town has no fact-checkers of its own — lies are caught less often.
townGen.rules/rich/text: Higher wages: people spend more, and shops and bars hold on more easily.
townGen.rules/clingy/text: The City Voice prints one more story.
townGen.rules/crime/text: Crime is higher from day one.
townGen.goals/gang/name: Hand the streets to a gang

upgrades.kiosk_1/description: One more point of sale by the market: +7% reach — more people see the paper and pick it up.
upgrades.kiosk_2/description: One more point of sale by the factory gates: +7% reach — more people see the paper and pick it up.
upgrades.kiosk_3/description: One more point of sale at the bus stop: +7% reach — more people see the paper and pick it up.
upgrades.kiosk_4/description: One more point of sale by the hospital: +7% reach — more people see the paper and pick it up.
upgrades.subscription/description: The paper is brought home: readers drop it 25% less often.
upgrades.paid_subscription/description: Subscribers hardly ever drop the paper: they leave half as often.
upgrades.paid_subscription/drawback: Almost half as many new readers come.
upgrades.newspaper_quality_1/description: The paper looks more serious: +15% reach, +5 reputation.
upgrades.newspaper_quality_2/description: Read for his opinions: +20% reach, +5 reputation.
upgrades.tv_guide/description: Pensioners pick up the paper more often: their interest +0.15.
upgrades.sports_page/description: Football and fishing: workers start buying the paper (interest +0.3).
upgrades.youth_insert/description: Comics, horoscope and listings: young people pick up the paper (interest +0.35).
upgrades.photographer/description: Photos on the front page: it's read 20% more often.
upgrades.photographer/drawback: Not everyone likes such photos: readers drop the paper 5% more often.
upgrades.trolls/description: Scary stories are passed on 40% more readily.
upgrades.trolls/drawback: A caught lie costs 20% more reputation.
upgrades.mole/description: Your own person in the rival's newsroom: you see what it will print today.
upgrades.mole/drawback: Each day there's a 5% chance the mole is uncovered: −5% reputation, and the mole is gone.
upgrades.night_shift/description: Trick: one reporter brings one more story today.
upgrades.sensation_day/description: Trick: the day's best story gets one level stronger (up to a sensation).
upgrades.crime_desk/description: Your own crime reporter: reporters bring crime more often, and crime stories hit 30% harder.
upgrades.crime_desk/drawback: Readers who don't care for the topic drop the paper 5% more often.
upgrades.factory_desk/description: A person at the gates: stories about the factory hit 30% harder.
upgrades.factory_desk/drawback: Readers who don't care for the topic drop the paper 5% more often.
upgrades.health_desk/description: The paper's own “doctor”: health stories hit 30% harder.
upgrades.health_desk/drawback: Readers who don't care for the topic drop the paper 5% more often.
upgrades.power_desk/description: Your own person in the mayor's office: stories about the authorities hit 30% harder.
upgrades.power_desk/drawback: Readers who don't care for the topic drop the paper 5% more often.
upgrades.dossier/description: A file on everyone: a smear speeds up one and a half times faster — each day in a row adds more to the hit.
upgrades.insiders/description: People in every building: reporters bring stories about the smear's target noticeably more often.
upgrades.insiders/drawback: Word of the “thank-yous” gets around: −2 reputation with everyone.
upgrades.interceptors/description: We hand out the paper by the Voice's kiosks: an interesting issue takes twice as many of its readers.
upgrades.interceptors/drawback: Fewer of your own kiosks: readers drop the paper 5% more often.
upgrades.cartoonist/description: Nasty cartoons with the news: they're passed on 25% more readily.
upgrades.gate_handout/description: The paper is pushed into workers' hands after their shift: workers buy it more readily.
upgrades.gate_handout/drawback: What comes free is easy to drop: readers leave 5% more often.
upgrades.proofreader/description: Cleans up the traces: lies are caught 15% less often.
upgrades.proofreader/drawback: He edits the truth too: it brings 10% less reputation.
upgrades.newsboys/description: They shout the headlines on every corner: people pick up the paper more often.
upgrades.job_ads/description: Job ads: workers pick up the paper more readily (interest +0.15).
upgrades.police_scanner/description: A free reporter often heads where trouble struck: more crime stories.
upgrades.gossip_column/description: Stories are passed on more readily.
upgrades.gossip_column/drawback: The truth earns a little less reputation.
upgrades.archive/description: Old bound volumes: investigations take a day less.
upgrades.interns/description: Interns run the errands: dirty tricks cool down a day sooner.
upgrades.angry_letters/description: Letters from angry townsfolk: stoked quarrels flare up harder.
upgrades.bar_regulars/description: They hear everything first: stories about the smear's target come more often.
upgrades.sponsor/description: A sponsor pays for an extra run: 25% more new readers.
upgrades.sponsor/drawback: The townsfolk sense it: −3 reputation with everyone.
upgrades.night_patrol/description: A reporter rides with the patrol: crime stories hit harder and heat the town more.
upgrades.provocateurs/description: Your people in the crowd: clashes between groups happen noticeably more often.
upgrades.provocateurs/drawback: If it comes out — scandal: checks 5% stricter.
upgrades.smear_lab/description: Investigations are a day faster, and a smear picks up speed 15% faster.
upgrades.epidemiologist/description: Stories about health and food hit harder.
upgrades.defectors/description: The Voice's writers ask to join us: you can lure them more often — a 40% shorter wait.
upgrades.press_cards/description: Reporters get in everywhere: luck +0.08, lies are checked a little more gently.
upgrades.health_inspector/description: Your person at the sanitary inspectorate: a smear leaves a 40% bigger stain.
upgrades.radio_ads/drawback: Pushy ads annoy people: −2 reputation with everyone.
upgrades.factchecker_friend/description: Warns you in advance: an exposure costs 20% less reputation, checks are gentler.
upgrades.holding_lawyer/description: Any exposure costs half the reputation, and the fact-checkers are more careful.
upgrades.city_hall_leaks/description: Stories about the authorities hit 40% harder; quarrels flare harder and more often.
upgrades.gang_contact/description: Crime stories heat the town twice as much; reporters write about crime more often.
upgrades.tabloid_king/description: Scary stories hit 30% harder and are passed on 30% more often.
upgrades.media_baron/description: The holding invests: +8% reach and 20% more new readers.
upgrades.smear_machine/description: A smear leaves a 60% bigger stain and speeds up twice as fast.
upgrades.informant/description: Opens the dirty trick “Buy a leak”: a sensation goes straight into the issue.
upgrades.informant/drawback: Each leak costs reputation, and with a 25% chance it's a setup.
upgrades.fact_friend/description: Opens the dirty trick “Grease the fact-checkers”: that day lies are checked five times less often.
upgrades.fact_friend/drawback: Each envelope costs reputation; old lies surface as usual.
upgrades.hired_crowd/description: Opens the dirty trick “Hire provocateurs”: the next day the tensest pair of groups is sure to clash.
upgrades.paparazzi_team/description: Opens the dirty trick “Paparazzi”: the next day there's sure to be a story about the smear's target.
upgrades.paparazzi_team/drawback: Without a smear the trick doesn't work.
upgrades.free_run/description: Opens the dirty trick “Hand out the paper free”: the day's issue is read by the whole town.

cards.factory_accident/titles/1: Factory covers up a string of accidents
cards.factory_accident/titles/2: Workers are choking and dying at the factory
cards.factory_accident/softTitles/0: Factory accident minor: no one hurt
cards.price_rise/titles/0: Food prices go up in the shops
cards.price_rise/softTitles/0: Price rise is temporary: cheaper by summer
cards.price_rise/softTitles/1: Town's prices the lowest in the region
cards.new_bar/titles/0: The bar launches a new evening programme
cards.new_bar/titles/1: Criminals drop into the bar at night
cards.new_bar/titles/2: The bar is poisoning its customers
cards.hospital_queue/titles/1: Doctors can't cope with the flood of patients
cards.hospital_queue/titles/2: Epidemic in town, hospital hides the figures
cards.hospital_queue/softTitles/1: Hospital sees patients with no queues
cards.mayor_promise/titles/2: Mayor is stealing the town budget
cards.factory_bonus/titles/2: Factory hasn't paid wages for three months
cards.festival/titles/2: Mass brawl with victims at the festival
cards.shop_layoff/titles/2: All the shops will close soon
cards.shop_layoff/softTitles/0: Laid-off shop staff already found new jobs
cards.sports_win/titles/2: Match was fixed, team to be disbanded
cards.water_poison/titles/2: Poison found in the water supply
cards.factory_sold/titles/1: Factory to be sold to outsiders
cards.factory_sold/titles/2: Factory to close as early as next month
cards.shop_rats/titles/1: Rats spotted in the market shop
cards.shop_rats/titles/2: Food in the shops is contaminated
cards.mayor_flee/titles/1: Mayor seen with suitcases at the station
cards.mayor_flee/titles/2: Mayor preparing to flee town with the treasury
cards.crime_wave/titles/2: A gang roams the town, police do nothing
cards.bar_drugs/titles/1: Banned substances sold at the bar
cards.bar_drugs/titles/2: Young people poisoned en masse in bars
cards.layoffs_coming/titles/2: Half the workers to be fired by the end of the week
cards.tax_rise/titles/1: Town hall discusses a new tax
cards.tax_rise/titles/2: Town hall will take the townsfolk's last penny
cards.celebrity/titles/1: They say a star is coming to town
cards.celebrity/titles/2: A star has secretly arrived in town
cards.global_recession/titles/1: The crisis will hit every family
cards.global_recession/titles/2: Country on the brink of default, savings will burn
cards.global_recession/softTitles/0: National downturn will pass our town by
cards.global_recession/softTitles/1: The national economy is booming like never before
cards.global_grain/titles/1: Bread will soon be a luxury
cards.global_grain/titles/2: Food will vanish from shelves nationwide
cards.global_grain/softTitles/0: Grain prices won't touch us: stocks are enough
cards.global_star/titles/0: Pop star releases a new album
cards.global_star/titles/2: Pop star dies in mysterious circumstances
cards.global_flu/titles/1: Flu outbreak in a neighbouring country
cards.global_flu/titles/2: A deadly virus is already heading our way
cards.global_plants/titles/2: Our factory is next on the closure list
cards.global_taxes/titles/2: Taxes to double this very month
cards.global_aliens/titles/1: Strange lights seen over a neighbouring town
